new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C10.md Theorem 2); recurrence equals brute force for m <= 24
new.statement:
The total number of digit changes when counting from 0 to G_m - 1 in the Zeckendorf system (G = 1,2,3,5,...)
is T_m = 2 G_m - ceil(m/2) - 2, satisfying T_(m+1) = T_m + T_(m-1) + ceil(m/2) + 1; the average cost of
Zeckendorf counting tends to 2.
new.title: Zeckendorf counting: T_m = 2 G_m - ceil(m/2) - 2, average cost 2

new.counterexample: Both averages tend to exactly 2 (Theorem 2 and the binary case of Theorem 1); at n < 1e6 the Zeckendorf average is 1.999992 vs binary 1.999988.
new.statement: The average number of digit changes per increment in the Zeckendorf system is smaller than in binary.
new.title: H-C10-0: Zeckendorf counting is cheaper than binary counting (refuted)

new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C10.md Theorem 3) from the abelian property (CLM-C02-02); deviation <= 5.7e-4 at n = 2e5 for all 31 rules
new.statement: For every terminating carry rule (m; b) the average number of firings per increment tends to 1/(m - sum_j b_j).
new.title: Exchange systems fire 1/(m - sum b) times per increment on average

new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C10.md Theorem 4); deviation <= 2.7e-4 for all single-offset rules
new.statement: If the carry rule has a single nonzero b_g = q < m, every increment changes exactly (number of firings) + 1 digits; the average cost is 1 + 1/(m - q).
new.title: Single-offset exchange rules cost exactly firings + 1 per increment (average 1 + 1/(m - q))

new.limitations: Averages over 2e5 increments only; no formula.
new.statement:
For carry rules with two or more nonzero b_j, the average digit-change cost per increment converges to a
constant exceeding 1 + 1/(m - B) (measured excess: 0.500 for 3->(1,1), 0.333 for 4->(1,1), 0.643 for
3->(0,1,1), 0.714 for 3->(1,0,1), 0.831 for 4->(1,1,1)), equal to an expectation under the invariant measure of
the digit process.
new.title: Multi-offset exchange rules have rule-specific average counting costs

new.novelty_basis: Myers (1983), Okasaki (skew binary random-access lists).
new.statement: In canonical skew binary, every increment changes at most 2 digits and the average is 3/2 (n < 1e6).
new.title: Skew binary counting has worst-case cost 2 and average 3/2

new: All classical constants confirmed to 5-6 digits; Zeckendorf averages 2 like binary; skew binary has worst case 2.
The block recurrence matches brute force; D_m = ceil(m/2) + 2 exactly.
Average firings match 1/(m - B) for all 31 rules; single-offset rules cost exactly firings + 1; multi-offset rules carry an extra rule-dependent cost.
